key_insight: Privacy-preserving distillation can transfer LLM clinical reasoning into compact models for multimorbidity scoring without using real patient data.
clinical_relevance: The distilled scores improved survival prediction in UK Biobank, suggesting a scalable way to support risk stratification in population health research.
method: Used teacher LLMs to generate multimorbidity reasoning on synthetic cohorts that match UK Biobank distributions.
Distilled this knowledge into compact student models (CoLLMs) designed to preserve privacy.
Evaluated transfer quality and clinical usefulness with LLM-as-Judge and downstream prediction tests.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong knowledge transfer (Spearman rho 0.75–0.89), survival prediction performance up to C-index 0.91, and higher SNP heritability (h2 approx. 0.05).
watch_item: Performance and clinical value may vary across teacher models, so validation and governance are needed before broader deployment.
paper_title: Privacy-Aware Distillation of Large Language Models for Enhanced Multimorbidity Scoring
